Follow-up recorded by AI-0074 (bitty-ai): extend the secret-scan CI gate to the docs repositories. Governance authority: specifications/governance-rfc.md (gitleaks as a pre-merge gate, R-014/R-019).

Port the canonical implementation from bitty-ai commit f1a435d (read-only reference: git -C $BITTY_WORKSPACE/bitty-ai show f1a435d:.github/workflows/ci.yml and ...:justfile) to this repository, adapting to this repo own pins and toolchain:
1. justfile: add gitleaks_version := "8.30.1" as the single source of truth; add a secrets recipe (gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner) and a gitleaks-version recipe that reports pinned vs local and must not fail on a build without ldflags version metadata.
2. .github/workflows/ci.yml: add a job id secrets, name Secret scan, ubuntu-latest, timeout-minutes: 15, checkout with this repo existing pinned SHA and fetch-depth: 0; an Install checksum-verified gitleaks step that derives the version from the justfile pin (fail-closed when empty), downloads the pinned release tarball plus checksums file, verifies with sha256sum --check --strict, extracts, installs into $HOME/.local/bin and appends it to GITHUB_PATH; then gitleaks detect --source . --no-banner.
3. Keep secrets OUT of the check recipe; no gitleaks-action, no pull_request_target, no new permissions or secrets; keep workflow-level contents: read.
4. Run the scan on this repo history; if it reports false positives, add a minimal .gitleaks.toml with narrowly scoped anchored-path allowlists and record the evidence; otherwise no config file.

Evidence: actionlint on ci.yml, act -n dry run showing the Secret scan job, just secrets result, negative-control check, just check + git diff --check.
title: CI secret-scan gate: pin gitleaks and add a checksum-verified Secret scan job

description: Record the user's Panel/Workspace interaction design as a candidate specification. Issue: #77. DELIVERABLE: new documents in the terminal-docs corpus (suggested specifications/panel-workspace-interaction-candidate.md, status draft, website_publish: false, document_type: specification, non-colliding sidebar_order) recording: (1) Mod+left-drag Panel repositioning inside a Workspace with free resize between very small and very large, never leaving the Bitty surface; (2) Mod+V floating Panel toggle overlaying other Panels but confined to the Bitty terminal; (3) animations for open/close, move, resize, workspace switch, float toggle; (4) Bar configurability: edge position top/bottom/left/right, height, colors, slider/indicator color, animations, active-workspace color, hideable, and the Workspace area it occupies; (5) stable unique identifiers for Panels and Workspaces (not 0,1,2,3) where Mod+Number changes only the physical display position and identity persists across moves/switch/restart; (6) every Workspace has at least one Panel, no empty Workspace; (7) Panel moves across Workspaces via Mod+Shift+Number or manual drag; (8) drag-to-Bar semantics: drop on a slider center moves the Panel to that Workspace and switches to it, drop near a slider's left/right edge creates a new single-Panel Workspace at that position (tiling-WM semantics); (9) all behaviors exposed to Lua through a capability-gated API, bounded by the accepted security posture.
